title: Tiered solver emitting a Solve Trace
description:
Replace the boolean canSolveLogically with a solver that resolves ONE cell at a time by the lowest applicable Tier, recording per Step: cell, symbol, Tier used, and how many other cells were deducible at that moment.

Tiers:
1 Direct - consecutive patterns (XX_, _XX, X_X), Constraint Marker with a filled neighbour, line already holding three of one symbol.
2 Line enumeration - enumerate the 14 legal 6-cell line patterns filtered by filled cells and internal Constraint Markers; any cell identical across all survivors is forced. Exact, and subsumes findNakedPairsMoves, findAdvancedPatternMoves and findBalanceMoves - those three get deleted.
3 Cross-line propagation - intersect line candidate sets at shared row/column cells, iterate to fixpoint.
4 Depth-one contradiction - assume a value, run tiers 1-3, contradiction forces the other. Depth 1 ONLY; depth >= 2 is guessing and must be rejected.

Batch application must go: it makes Narrowness and Bottlenecks unmeasurable.
acceptance_criteria: Solver returns a Solve Trace; findNakedPairsMoves, findAdvancedPatternMoves, findBalanceMoves and sortMovesByReliability deleted; existing puzzles still solve.
close_reason: Added a one-cell-at-a-time solve trace with four tiers, exact valid-line enumeration, cross-line candidates, and depth-one contradiction. Removed the old advanced, naked-pair, balance and priority heuristics. Direct trace and normal generator compatibility checks passed.

title: Remove unsound row/column uniqueness technique from LogicalSolver
description:
findUniqueRowsColumnsMoves in frontend/src/lib/game/solvers/LogicalSolver.ts deduces from a 'no two identical rows/columns' rule that Tango does not have. BoardValidator only enforces the balance and no-three-consecutive rules. 47.7% of the 11,222 valid Solution Grids contain a duplicated row, so this is not a corner case.

Impact: when an unsound deduction contradicts the true solution, canSolveLogically rejects a legal removal (blander puzzles, invisible). When it coincides with the solution by luck, the removal is ACCEPTED and we certify as 'logically solvable' a puzzle that is not deducible from the rules the player has. Uniqueness still passes because it is checked by a separate real solver, so we ship a guessing puzzle.

Also delete findDifferences, which only this technique uses and which is separately broken: it pushes two entries per differing column, so the guard 'differences.length === 2' tests for ONE differing position, not two, and it counts a column as differing when either cell is merely EMPTY.

Independent of the generator redesign and shippable now.
acceptance_criteria: findUniqueRowsColumnsMoves and findDifferences deleted; no remaining caller; puzzles still generate.
close_reason: Removed the unsupported uniqueness technique and its only helper; no callers remain. Direct solver check passed.

title: Per-Player Stream: seeded permutation of the Bank plus a counter
description:
A Player (browser profile) gets a UUID and an integer counter in localStorage. Puzzle n is the nth entry of a permutation of the Bank seeded from the UUID. Past the end of the Bank, fall through to the runtime generator in a Web Worker.

The no-repeat guarantee holds by construction: only a counter is persisted, never a seen-set, so partial data loss can only skip forward. Call navigator.storage.persist() on load - Safari deletes script-writable storage after seven days without user interaction, which would silently reset a returning Player.

See docs/adr/0001.
acceptance_criteria: Two fresh Players get different orderings; a Player never repeats a Puzzle Instance; persist() called on load.
close_reason: Added deterministic seeded permutations per Player and Band with persistent UUID/counters, hard exhaustion protection, and navigator.storage.persist() request. Focused stream test and browser verification pass.

title: Collapse five Bands into three measured ones
description:
PUZZLE_CONFIGS in frontend/src/lib/game/types.ts defines five difficulties. 'easy' and 'hard' are byte-for-byte identical; 'medium' and 'expert' differ only in constraintProbability, which is dead on the main path (only createFallbackPuzzle reads it, via addStrategicConstraints).

Replace with three Bands - Easy, Medium, Hard - assigned from the highest Tier a puzzle requires, not from Given counts. startingPiecesMin/Max and constraintProbability stop being generation inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Three Bands; no Given-count or constraint-probability dials driving generation; scoring/par values reassigned.
close_reason: Replaced five legacy clue-count/constraint-probability difficulties with score-only Easy, Medium, and Hard Bands. Bank selection now uses measured solve tier: 1, 2, and 3-4 respectively. Typecheck and production build pass.

title: Offline Bank builder
description:
A tsx script importing the SAME solver modules the game uses - never a second copy of the solving logic. Generates candidates, scores them from the Solve Trace, filters, and emits ~10k Puzzle Instances as JSON into frontend/static/.

Minimality is a HARD filter, not a score term. Emit raw trace metrics per puzzle and keep the weighting in a separate config that can change without regenerating. Prefer unused Solution Grids when picking, so early puzzles are grid-distinct as well as instance-distinct.

~24 bytes per puzzle encoded; 10k should be under 100KB gzipped.
acceptance_criteria: Bank JSON produced; every entry minimal, uniquely solvable, requires no more than Tier 4; raw metrics present per entry.
notes: Playtest milestone committed: local new-game flow now serves the 100-entry static Bank, verified in Vite with decoded givens/markers matching bank.json. Keep this issue open to curate the planned ~10,000-entry release Bank.
close_reason: Built and validated 10,000 compact Puzzle Instances. All IDs are unique, entries have valid dimensions and raw metrics, and each passed the Bank builder's uniqueness, minimality, trace-solvability and Tier <=4 filters. Asset is 3.12 MB raw / 326 KB gzip.

title: Baseline: score the current generator's output
description: Before changing generation, run the trace-emitting solver over a large sample of puzzles from the CURRENT generator and record Band distribution, Narrowness, Bottleneck counts and minimality. Nothing about 'more interesting' is falsifiable without this baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline metrics recorded and committed so later generators can be compared against them.
close_reason: Recorded 20 deterministic samples for each current band with shared trace, narrowness, bottleneck, uniqueness, and minimality metrics. All 100 are unique and solvable; only 45 are minimal and no sample requires Tier 3.

title: Rebuild puzzle generation around measured difficulty
description:
Difficulty is currently an input dial (Given count + constraint probability) rather than a measured property. Five Bands exist, two of which are byte-identical. Constraint Markers are local patches bolted on to rescue random removals, which manufactures shallow deductions.

Replace the boolean solvability oracle with a Solve Trace, rate puzzles from it, and move generation to generate-and-filter against a Bank built offline.

See CONTEXT.md for vocabulary and docs/adr/0001 and 0002 for the decisions.
close_reason: All six child tasks are complete: sound solver, solve traces, baseline, candidate comparison, curated Bank, measured Bands, and a per-Player non-repeating stream.

title: Candidate generators: random-dig, constraint-first, symmetric
description:
Several cheap generators feeding one expensive scorer, so the data says which one produces puzzles we like rather than us guessing. Targeted construction (build a puzzle that forces technique X at step Y) is unsolved and is NOT what this is - all candidates get scored and filtered.

Constraint-first places a coherent Constraint Marker set before removing cells, instead of patching markers in to rescue removals as the current generator does.
acceptance_criteria: At least two generators implemented behind a common interface; scored output compared.
close_reason: Added a common candidate-generator interface and compared 20 deterministic Medium candidates from random-dig and constraint-first using the shared metrics. Both are unique and solvable; constraint-first is currently non-minimal, which the Bank filter will reject.

title: Fix Timeout vs number type error in gameStore timerInterval
description:
svelte-check fails on frontend/src/lib/stores/gameStore.svelte.ts:147 - 'Type Timeout is not assignable to type number'. setInterval resolves to the Node overload rather than the DOM one. Pre-existing; the only error left in the tree.

Fix is either to type the handle as ReturnType<typeof setInterval> or to stop pulling @types/node into the browser tsconfig.
acceptance_criteria: npm run check passes with zero errors.
close_reason: timerInterval now uses ReturnType<typeof setInterval>; npm run check reports zero errors.

title: Delete the dead backend API client
description: frontend/src/lib/api/gameApi.ts fetches ${API_BASE_URL}/api/game/* against a Python backend that no longer exists. Nothing in the live path calls it - GameService does everything client-side and the app deploys static to GitHub Pages. Misleading to a reader given we have decided against a backend entirely (docs/adr/0001).
close_reason: Removed unreferenced gameApi.ts; no GameApi/API_BASE_URL/ApiError references remain. Typecheck and production build pass.
